title: Socio-Ecological Assessment of Elderly Primary Healthcare Accessibility in China Using the Vegetation Nighttime Condition Index and the Enhanced 2SFCA

idea.research_question: How does an ecologically constrained human-activity signal relate to spatial accessibility of primary healthcare for older adults?
idea.hypothesis: The fused VIIRS-NDVI signal reveals socio-ecological context, while age-specific population demand exposes healthcare-accessibility mismatches.
idea.mechanism: Vegetation Nighttime Condition Index, enhanced 2SFCA, network travel impedance and coupling-coordination analysis
idea.expected_contribution: Transfers remote-sensing indicators into age-specific healthcare equity analysis.
idea.falsification_condition: Reject if any required role is omitted, background-only, or not operationally used in the same research instance.

anchor_context.extraction_basis: Full-text seed evidence; empirical results are excluded from the task prompt.
